app.name: LinkedIn Ads
app.review_note: Checked against provider sources on 2 November 2026; corrections are listed in VERIFICATION.md.

summary.headline: LinkedIn Ads API access is by application: request the Advertising API, build in the Development tier, and request Standard tier with a demo video only if you need many ad accounts.
summary.type_note: Access starts in the Development tier after approval. Standard tier is only needed for campaign management across multiple ad accounts and needs a video and LinkedIn's approval.

difficulty_factors.reason: Creating a developer app requires an active LinkedIn account and an existing LinkedIn Company Page to link to the application.
Production (Standard tier) requires human review and submission of a demo video showing the app creating, editing, or optimizing LinkedIn campaigns.
Neither Development-tier approval nor Standard-tier review has a published turnaround.
The sources checked mention no platform fee, but you need an ad account with an administrative role.
A human reviewer must manually evaluate the application and review the video demonstration before Standard tier access is granted.

setup_effort.estimate: About 1-2 hours for the Development tier once access is granted (estimate); several days to produce the demo video

approval_wait.label: Unknown: no published turnaround for Development-tier approval or Standard review

can_start_today.reason: You can register an app and request the Advertising API product today, but access depends on LinkedIn approving your application.

confidence.reason: Tier structure and scopes come from Microsoft Learn. Approval timing and the Company Page requirement could not be verified.

blockers.title: Advertising API access is by application
blockers.detail: The Advertising API is for approved developers, and LinkedIn reserves the right to review applications at its discretion.
blockers.workaround: Apply with a clear use case and use the Developer Support Portal if you hear nothing.

blockers.title: A LinkedIn Company Page may be required
blockers.detail: An earlier version of this guide stated that creating an app needs a Company Page where you are an administrator. This was not independently verified.
blockers.workaround: Create a Company Page if the app form asks for one.

blockers.title: Development tier limits
blockers.detail: Development tier allows unlimited reads for ad accounts you administer but edits for only up to five ad accounts. Ad accounts are added under Products, then View Ad Accounts.
blockers.workaround: Copy your nine-digit Ad Account ID from Campaign Manager and add it in the Developer Portal.

blockers.title: Standard tier is only needed for multi-account campaign management
blockers.detail: Standard tier needs a demo video, and LinkedIn may decline even qualified requests. LinkedIn's FAQ says you do not need it unless you build campaign management for multiple ad accounts.
blockers.workaround: Stay on Development tier if five editable ad accounts are enough.

steps.title: Create a LinkedIn Company Page
steps.action: Ensure you have an existing LinkedIn Company Page where you are an Administrator. If you do not have one, create a Company Page via LinkedIn.
steps.why_human_only: Requires an authenticated LinkedIn user account and organization details.

steps.title: Register Application on LinkedIn Developer Portal
steps.action: Navigate to the LinkedIn Developer Portal, click 'Create App', provide an App Name, associate your LinkedIn Company Page, upload an App Logo, and agree to the Developer API Terms of Use.

fields.name: App name
fields.guidance: Enter your product or AI agent integration name

fields.name: LinkedIn Page
fields.guidance: Select your verified LinkedIn Company Page URL or name

steps.why_human_only: Requires personal LinkedIn authentication and acceptance of legal terms.

steps.title: Configure OAuth 2.0 Redirect URLs
steps.action: Go to the 'Auth' tab of your application in the LinkedIn Developer Portal. Note your Client ID and Client Secret, and register your absolute HTTPS redirect callback URLs under OAuth 2.0 settings.

fields.name: Authorized redirect URLs for your app
fields.guidance: Absolute HTTPS callback URL (e.g., https://yourdomain.com/api/auth/linkedin/callback). Cannot contain URL fragments (#) or query parameters.

steps.title: Add Advertising API Product
steps.action: Open the Products tab of your app, find Advertising API and request it, completing the access form with your use case. Once approved, your app starts in the Development tier.

steps.title: Map Test Ad Accounts to Development Tier
steps.action: In Campaign Manager, copy your nine-digit Ad Account ID. In the Developer Portal under the app's Products tab, click 'View Ad Accounts', choose 'Add Ad Account', enter the ID, and save.

fields.name: Ad Account ID
fields.guidance: Nine-digit Sponsored Account ID copied from Campaign Manager

steps.why_human_only: Requires Campaign Manager access and Developer Portal settings modification.

steps.title: Implement and Test 3-Legged OAuth Flow
steps.action: Initiate authorization redirect to https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, and desired scopes (e.g. r_ads, r_ads_reporting). Exchange authorization code for token at https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/accessToken.

steps.title: Apply for Advertising API Standard Tier
steps.action: Once your integration is built and tested, use the 'sending us an email' link in the Marketing Developer Platform settings (subject 'Standard API Access') or open a ticket on the Developer Support Portal. Include a video showing how your platform creates, edits or optimizes campaigns.

fields.name: Demo Video Link
fields.guidance: Public or unlisted video demonstrating campaign creation, management, or reporting workflows

fields.name: Use Case Description
fields.guidance: Detailed explanation of your platform's features and adherence to LinkedIn advertising policies

scopes.purpose: Read authenticated member's ad accounts and retrieve sponsored account metadata.
Retrieve analytics and reporting metrics for advertising accounts and campaigns.
Read and write access to manage ad campaigns, creatives, targeting, and budgets.
Verify administrative permissions on LinkedIn Company Pages associated with ad campaigns.
Manage LinkedIn Company Page settings and direct sponsored content.

common_rejection_reasons.reason: Standard tier request without a working integration or a video showing campaigns being created, edited or optimized
common_rejection_reasons.fix: Build and test in the Development tier first, then record a screen recording of the working flow.

common_rejection_reasons.reason: Target ad account not on the app's ad account list, giving 403 errors
common_rejection_reasons.fix: Add the nine-digit Ad Account ID under Products, then View Ad Accounts, and make sure your user has an adequate role on the account.

common_rejection_reasons.reason: Request declined at LinkedIn's discretion even when requirements are met
common_rejection_reasons.fix: Ask for feedback through the Developer Support Portal and resubmit with a clearer demo.

message_template.subject: Standard API Access: {{app_name}}
message_template.body:
Hello LinkedIn Developer Support Team,

We are requesting Standard API Access for {{app_name}} (App ID: {{client_id}}).

We built and tested campaign and reporting workflows in the Development tier using our ad account (ID: {{ad_account_id}}). Our demo video is here: {{demo_video_url}}.

Could you tell us if any additional technical or compliance information is needed?

Best regards,
{{developer_name}}
{{company_name}}

Probed and parsed Microsoft Learn official documentation for LinkedIn Marketing Developer Platform, Quick Start, Increasing Access, and 3-Legged OAuth Flow
agent_can_do_next: Draft OAuth 2.0 authorization URL and token exchange handler implementation code
Draft API request payloads for LinkedIn Ad Accounts, Campaign Management, and Ad Analytics endpoints
Validate redirect URI formatting and required scope query strings

you_must.task: Sign in to LinkedIn and verify ownership or admin access on a LinkedIn Company Page
you_must.reason: LinkedIn Developer Portal requires linking an existing Company Page to register an application.

you_must.task: Create the app in the LinkedIn Developer Portal and retrieve Client ID and Client Secret
you_must.reason: Creating apps and accessing secret credentials cannot be automated without user authentication.

you_must.task: Add the Advertising API product and map your 9-digit Ad Account ID
you_must.reason: Development tier only permits API calls against explicitly mapped ad accounts.

you_must.task: Record and submit the demo video for Standard tier access
you_must.reason: Standard tier requires a visual walkthrough of your working integration before approving external member access.

evidence.claim: LinkedIn OAuth 2.0 authorization and token endpoints are https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization and https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/accessToken.
evidence.source_note: OpenID configuration returns authorization_endpoint and token_endpoint on linkedin.com.

evidence.claim: LinkedIn 3-legged OAuth requires absolute HTTPS redirect URLs with no query parameters or fragment identifiers.
evidence.source_note: LinkedIn 3-Legged OAuth Flow documentation specifies redirect URLs must be absolute HTTPS, ignore query params, and forbid hash fragments.

evidence.claim: Ad Accounts and Company Pages are managed entities with specific administrative roles, and Ad Account users can be queried and managed via the API.
evidence.source_note: Documentation outlines Company Page and Ad Account concepts, roles like ACCOUNT_BILLING_ADMIN, and Campaign Manager usage.

evidence.claim: To upgrade to Standard tier, build and test your application first, then submit a tier upgrade request including a video showing how your platform creates, edits and/or optimizes campaigns.
evidence.source_note: Marketing quick start. Earlier wording about Company Pages and ad account mapping was removed because it was not supported by this source.

evidence.claim: The Advertising API product grants permissions including r_ads, rw_ads, r_ads_reporting, r_organization_admin, and rw_organization_admin.
evidence.source_note: Increasing Access guide lists all granted OAuth permissions for Advertising API and details General Availability vs restricted programs.

evidence.claim: Reporting API requires r_ads to read ad accounts and r_ads_reporting to retrieve campaign analytics.
evidence.source_note: Reporting documentation details required scopes r_ads and r_ads_reporting.

evidence.claim: LinkedIn authorization endpoint rejects invalid client IDs with an explicit error message.
evidence.source_note: Probed authorize endpoint with fake_client_12345; responded with status 200 and text 'The passed in client_id is invalid "fake_client_12345"'.

evidence.claim: Standard access is requested through a link to email with the subject 'Standard API Access', with a demo video; LinkedIn may decline even qualified applicants. The Advertising API product is applied for on the app's Products tab.
evidence.source_note: Microsoft Learn: LinkedIn Marketing API program access tiers.

evidence.claim: The Advertising API is open to approved developers. Development tier allows unlimited reads for ad accounts you administer and edits for up to five; Standard access is requested via a support ticket on the Developer Support Portal.
You do not need Standard tier for the Advertising API unless you build campaign management for multiple ad accounts; ad accounts are added under Products, then View Ad Accounts.
evidence.source_note: Marketing API FAQ (an older documentation version).

evidence.claim: No published turnaround for Development-tier approval or Standard-tier review was found.
evidence.source_note: Searched Microsoft Learn's LinkedIn Marketing docs.

evidence.claim: Whether a Company Page is required to create an app was not independently checked.
evidence.source_note: Carried over from the original guide.

unknowns.question: What is the review turnaround for Development-tier approval and for Standard tier?
unknowns.how_to_resolve: Submit the request and ask on the Developer Support Portal (https://www.linkedin.com/help/lms) if there is no reply after 10-14 business days.

unknowns.question: Is a Company Page required to create an app?
unknowns.how_to_resolve: Try creating an app in the Developer Portal.

unknowns.question: Do per-scope rules trigger extra review?
unknowns.why_unknown: The docs tie review to the access tier, not to individual scopes.
